Snapshot integrity: Contract.lean and Submission.lean in the snapshot are byte-identical to the workspace copies. The cited mathlib files are identical to the compiled lake package (commit 25730c7c). TendstoLocallyInL1On (SimonGMT BV.lean) means ∀ compact K ⊆ U, ∫⁻_K‖v_i − u‖ₑ → 0.

Library gaps:
- Mathlib has CompactExhaustion only for whole (σ-compact, locally compact) spaces. There is no lemma for an open subset that absorbs compact sets, so compact_exhaustion is new.
- Mathlib has no L¹ compactness theorem (no Kolmogorov–Riesz/Rellich/Fréchet–Kolmogorov match) and no gluing lemma for L¹_loc limits, so simultaneous_subseq and glue_limits are new.
- Their building blocks all exist and resolve: Lp completeness, Lp.edist_toLp_toLp/edist_def, eLpNorm_one_eq_lintegral_enorm, TotallyBounded.isCompact_of_isClosed, isCompact_univ_pi, the countable-product FirstCountableTopology instance, IsCompact.tendsto_subseq, locallyIntegrableOn_iff, IsCompact.elim_directed_cover and the infEDist API.
- In this mathlib eLpNorm_one_eq_lintegral_enorm needs AEStronglyMeasurable, and the child proofs account for this.

DAG check: no DAG node has an identical frozen type to reuse. eilenberg_compact_exhaustion and convex_open_exists_inner_exhaustion state different facts. The three new names are unreserved.

Lean checks: all three child types elaborate in the comparator scope and are proved outright with axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. The assembly from the three types to the exact frozen parent type, and the full chain, compile with the same axioms.

rationale:
Split into 3 independent children with no sibling dependencies. The selected node keeps a short assembly of about 10 lines. The supplied 9-step proof bundles three mathematically independent obligations that need disjoint tool sets. Each is a reusable lemma with no BV content.

(1) compact_exhaustion, from step 1 (metric topology). An open U ⊆ ℝⁿ has a monotone sequence of compact sets Q_j ⊆ U such that every compact K ⊆ U lies in some Q_j. Mathlib's CompactExhaustion covers only whole spaces, and the snapshot has no open-subset version.

(2) simultaneous_subseq, from steps 0 and 2–4 (L¹ functional analysis). Finite L¹ nets on countably many sets Q_j give one strictly increasing ψ and limits G_j, integrable on Q_j, with ∫⁻_{Q_j}‖u_{ψ(k)} − G_j‖ₑ → 0. The tools are Lp completeness, total boundedness, Tychonoff and sequential compactness. It is stated for arbitrary sets and uses only integrability and the nets.

(3) glue_limits, from steps 5–8 (a.e. measure theory). Limits on a monotone compact exhaustion that absorbs every compact subset of U glue to a v that is locally integrable on U, with TendstoLocallyInL1On.

Assembly. It is machine-checked, with axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]:
- intro n U u hU hloc hnet; obtain Q from (1);
- hint j k := (hloc k).integrableOn_compact_subset (hQU j) (hQc j);
- obtain ψ and G from (2) with the nets fun j ε hε ↦ hnet (Q j) (hQc j) (hQU j) ε hε;
- obtain v from (3) with w := fun k ↦ u (ψ k) and the measurability fun j k ↦ (hint j (ψ k)).aestronglyMeasurable;
- exact ⟨ψ, v, hψ, hv, htend⟩.

subproblems.title: Monotone compact exhaustion of an open subset of ℝⁿ that absorbs every compact subset (step 1 of the diagonal extraction)
subproblems.statement: For every n ∈ ℕ and every open set U ⊆ ℝⁿ (ℝⁿ = Rn n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) there are sets Q_j ⊆ ℝⁿ (j ∈ ℕ) such that: every Q_j is compact; Q_j ⊆ U for every j; Q_i ⊆ Q_j whenever i ≤ j (Q is monotone); and every compact set K ⊆ U is contained in some Q_j.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (U : Set (Rn n)), IsOpen U → ∃ Q : ℕ → Set (Rn n), (∀ j, IsCompact (Q j)) ∧ (∀ j, Q j ⊆ U) ∧ Monotone Q ∧ ∀ K : Set (Rn n), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ j, K ⊆ Q j
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2, Theorem 2.6 (p. 50). The printed proof reduces the claim to precompactness in L¹_loc(U), and the reviewed proof supplied to node root.bv_results-a1.compactness-a1.diagonal_subseq-a1 (step A2 of root.bv_results-a1.compactness-a1) turns precompactness on every compact subset into an L¹_loc-convergent subsequence by compact exhaustion and diagonal extraction. This child is step 1 of that proof (the compact exhaustion), extracted as a self-contained statement with the details filled in. Notation: ℝⁿ = Rn n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), a proper metric space; Uᶜ = ℝⁿ ∖ U; infEDist(x, A) = Metric.infEDist x A ∈ [0, ∞] (infEDist(x, ∅) = ∞); ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal.

Claim. If U ⊆ ℝⁿ is open, there are sets Q_j (j ∈ ℕ) with (i) every Q_j compact, (ii) Q_j ⊆ U, (iii) Q_i ⊆ Q_j for i ≤ j (Monotone Q), and (iv) every compact K ⊆ U contained in some Q_j.

1. Definition. For j ∈ ℕ put Q_j := closedBall(0, j + 1) ∩ {x : ofReal(1/(j + 1)) ≤ infEDist(x, Uᶜ)}. No case distinction is needed. If U = ℝⁿ then Uᶜ = ∅, infEDist(x, ∅) = ∞ and Q_j = closedBall(0, j + 1). If U = ∅ then infEDist(x, Uᶜ) = 0 < ofReal(1/(j + 1)) and every Q_j is empty. The case n = 0 is covered by the same argument.

2. Property (i), compactness. The function x ↦ infEDist(x, Uᶜ) is continuous: it is 1-Lipschitz (Metric.continuous_infEDist). Hence {x : ofReal(1/(j + 1)) ≤ infEDist(x, Uᶜ)} is closed (isClosed_le continuous_const continuous_infEDist). The ball closedBall(0, j + 1) is compact because ℝⁿ is proper (isCompact_closedBall). The intersection of a compact set with a closed set is compact (IsCompact.inter_right), so Q_j is compact.

3. Property (ii), Q_j ⊆ U. Let x ∈ Q_j and suppose x ∉ U. Then x ∈ Uᶜ, so infEDist(x, Uᶜ) = 0 (Metric.infEDist_zero_of_mem). But 1/(j + 1) > 0, so ofReal(1/(j + 1)) > 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_pos). This contradicts ofReal(1/(j + 1)) ≤ infEDist(x, Uᶜ) = 0. Hence x ∈ U.

4. Q_j ⊆ interior Q_{j+1}. Let x ∈ Q_j. Put O := ball(0, j + 2) ∩ {y : ofReal(1/(j + 2)) < infEDist(y, Uᶜ)}.
 (a) O is open. The ball is open, and the strict superlevel set of the continuous function y ↦ infEDist(y, Uᶜ) is open (isOpen_lt continuous_const continuous_infEDist).
 (b) x ∈ O. First, ‖x‖ ≤ j + 1 < j + 2. Second, 0 < 1/(j + 2) < 1/(j + 1) (one_div_lt_one_div_of_lt), so ofReal(1/(j + 2)) < ofReal(1/(j + 1)) (ENNReal.ofReal_lt_ofReal_iff). Since ofReal(1/(j + 1)) ≤ infEDist(x, Uᶜ), we get ofReal(1/(j + 2)) < infEDist(x, Uᶜ).
 (c) O ⊆ Q_{j+1}. Let y ∈ O. Then ‖y‖ < j + 2 = (j + 1) + 1, so y ∈ closedBall(0, (j + 1) + 1). Also ofReal(1/((j + 1) + 1)) = ofReal(1/(j + 2)) < infEDist(y, Uᶜ), so the inequality defining Q_{j+1} holds.
 So O is open and x ∈ O ⊆ Q_{j+1}, i.e. x ∈ interior Q_{j+1} (mem_interior).

5. Property (iii), monotonicity. By step 4 and interior Q_{j+1} ⊆ Q_{j+1} (interior_subset), Q_j ⊆ Q_{j+1} for every j. Induction on j − i gives Q_i ⊆ Q_j for all i ≤ j (monotone_nat_of_le_succ).

6. Every point of U lies in some Q_j. Let x ∈ U.
 (a) infEDist(x, Uᶜ) ≠ 0. Uᶜ is closed because U is open, so closure Uᶜ = Uᶜ (IsClosed.closure_eq). If infEDist(x, Uᶜ) = 0, then x ∈ closure Uᶜ = Uᶜ (Metric.mem_closure_iff_infEDist_zero), contradicting x ∈ U.
 (b) By ENNReal.exists_inv_nat_lt there is m ∈ ℕ with (m : [0,∞])⁻¹ < infEDist(x, Uᶜ).
 (c) Choose j ∈ ℕ with j ≥ max(‖x‖, m) (exists_nat_ge). Then ‖x‖ ≤ j + 1, so x ∈ closedBall(0, j + 1).
 (d) Since m ≤ j + 1, ofReal(1/(j + 1)) = ((j + 1 : [0,∞]))⁻¹ ≤ (m : [0,∞])⁻¹ < infEDist(x, Uᶜ). The lemmas are ENNReal.ofReal_inv_of_pos, ENNReal.ofReal_natCast and ENNReal.inv_le_inv. Hence x ∈ Q_j.

7. Property (iv), absorption of compact sets. Let K ⊆ U be compact. For j ∈ ℕ put V_j := interior Q_{j+1}.
 (a) Each V_j is open (isOpen_interior).
 (b) The V_j are increasing, so the family is directed: i ≤ j gives Q_{i+1} ⊆ Q_{j+1} by step 5, and interior is monotone (interior_mono).
 (c) The V_j cover K: each x ∈ K lies in U, hence in some Q_j by step 6, hence in V_j by step 4.
 (d) A compact set covered by a directed family of open sets lies in a single member of the family; the index type ℕ is nonempty (IsCompact.elim_directed_cover). So K ⊆ V_J for some J, and V_J ⊆ Q_{J+1}.

8. Steps 2, 3, 5 and 7 prove (i)–(iv) for Q = (Q_j)_{j∈ℕ}. ∎

(An equivalent Lean route: the subtype ↥U is locally compact (IsOpen.locallyCompactSpace) and σ-compact (second countable), so CompactExhaustion.choice ↥U exists, and its images under Subtype.val have properties (i)–(iv) by CompactExhaustion.exists_superset_of_isCompact. The explicit construction above is a complete proof on its own.)
proof_key_steps: Define Q_j := closedBall(0, j+1) ∩ {x : ofReal(1/(j+1)) ≤ infEDist(x, Uᶜ)}; the cases U = ℝⁿ, U = ∅ and n = 0 need no special treatment.
Q_j is compact: a compact closed ball meets the closed superlevel set of the continuous map x ↦ infEDist(x, Uᶜ).
Q_j ⊆ U: off U the distance infEDist(x, Uᶜ) is 0 < ofReal(1/(j+1)).
Q_j ⊆ interior Q_{j+1}: the open set ball(0, j+2) ∩ {ofReal(1/(j+2)) < infEDist(·, Uᶜ)} contains Q_j and lies in Q_{j+1}; hence Q is monotone.
Each x ∈ U lies in some Q_j: infEDist(x, Uᶜ) ≠ 0 because Uᶜ is closed, then choose j ≥ max(‖x‖, m) with m⁻¹ < infEDist(x, Uᶜ).
A compact K ⊆ U is covered by the increasing open sets interior Q_{j+1}; IsCompact.elim_directed_cover gives K ⊆ Q_{J+1}.

subproblems.title: Finite L¹ nets on countably many sets give one subsequence converging in L¹ on each of them (steps 0 and 2–4 of the diagonal extraction)
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, let Q_j ⊆ ℝⁿ (j ∈ ℕ) be arbitrary sets and u_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) functions such that every u_k is Lebesgue integrable on every Q_j, and such that for every j and every ε > 0 there is a finite set F ⊆ ℕ with: every k ∈ ℕ has some i ∈ F with ∫⁻_{Q_j} ‖u_k(x) − u_i(x)‖ₑ dx < ofReal ε. Then there are a strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ and functions G_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ (j ∈ ℕ) such that every G_j is integrable on Q_j and, for every j, ∫⁻_{Q_j} ‖u_{ψ(k)}(x) − G_j(x)‖ₑ dx → 0 as k → ∞.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (Q : ℕ → Set (Rn n)) (u : ℕ → Rn n → ℝ), (∀ j k, IntegrableOn (u k) (Q j) volume) → (∀ j, ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ F : Finset ℕ, ∀ k, ∃ i ∈ F, (∫⁻ x in Q j, ‖u k x - u i x‖ₑ) < ENNReal.ofReal ε) → ∃ (ψ : ℕ → ℕ) (G : ℕ → Rn n → ℝ), StrictMono ψ ∧ (∀ j, IntegrableOn (G j) (Q j) volume) ∧ ∀ j, Tendsto (fun k ↦ ∫⁻ x in Q j, ‖u (ψ k) x - G j x‖ₑ) atTop (𝓝 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2, Theorem 2.6 (p. 50). The printed proof reduces the claim to precompactness in L¹_loc(U), and the reviewed proof supplied to node root.bv_results-a1.compactness-a1.diagonal_subseq-a1 (step A2 of root.bv_results-a1.compactness-a1) turns precompactness on every compact subset into an L¹_loc-convergent subsequence by compact exhaustion and diagonal extraction. This child is steps 0 and 2–4 of that proof (the L¹ total boundedness and the extraction of one common subsequence), specialized to an arbitrary sequence of sets Q_j. Only two facts are used: each u_k is integrable on each Q_j, and the finite nets exist on each Q_j. Compactness and measurability of Q_j are not needed. Notation: μ = volume (Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ = Rn n); μ_j := μ.restrict Q_j; L_j := L¹(Q_j) := Lp ℝ 1 μ_j; ∫⁻_{Q_j} is the lower Lebesgue integral for μ_j; ‖a‖ₑ is the extended norm; ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal.

Claim. Assume (H1) every u_k is integrable on every Q_j, and (H2) for every j and every ε > 0 there is a finite F ⊆ ℕ such that every k has some i ∈ F with ∫⁻_{Q_j} ‖u_k − u_i‖ₑ < ofReal ε. Then there are a strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ and G_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ such that each G_j is integrable on Q_j and ∫⁻_{Q_j} ‖u_{ψ(k)} − G_j‖ₑ → 0 as k → ∞, for every j.

1. L¹ spaces. Each L_j is a complete metric space (Lp.instCompleteSpace). By (H1) and memLp_one_iff_integrable, u_k ∈ L¹(μ_j). Put f_{j,k} := [u_k]_{Q_j} := MemLp.toLp u_k ∈ L_j.

2. Distance formulas.
 (a) For all j, k, i: edist(f_{j,k}, f_{j,i}) = eLpNorm(u_k − u_i, 1, μ_j) (Lp.edist_toLp_toLp) = ∫⁻_{Q_j} ‖u_k − u_i‖ₑ (eLpNorm_one_eq_lintegral_enorm). That lemma needs u_k − u_i to be a.e.-strongly measurable for μ_j; this holds because u_k and u_i are integrable for μ_j by (H1). The hypothesis matters: in Mathlib the eLpNorm of a function that is not a.e.-strongly measurable is ∞.
 (b) Every g ∈ L_j has a representative ⇑g that is a.e.-strongly measurable and integrable for μ_j (Lp.aestronglyMeasurable, Lp.memLp, memLp_one_iff_integrable). For every k: edist(f_{j,k}, g) = eLpNorm(⇑f_{j,k} − ⇑g, 1, μ_j) (Lp.edist_def) = ∫⁻_{Q_j} ‖⇑f_{j,k} − ⇑g‖ₑ (eLpNorm_one_eq_lintegral_enorm, both terms a.e.-strongly measurable) = ∫⁻_{Q_j} ‖u_k − ⇑g‖ₑ. The last equality uses ⇑f_{j,k} = u_k μ_j-a.e. (MemLp.coeFn_toLp) and lintegral_congr_ae.

3. Total boundedness and compactness. Fix j. Let S_j := {f_{j,k} : k ∈ ℕ} and C_j := closure S_j ⊆ L_j.
 (a) S_j is totally bounded. Given ε > 0, take the finite F from (H2) for j and ε. Every k has some i ∈ F with ∫⁻_{Q_j} ‖u_k − u_i‖ₑ < ofReal ε, i.e. edist(f_{j,k}, f_{j,i}) < ofReal ε by 2(a). Hence dist(f_{j,k}, f_{j,i}) = (edist(f_{j,k}, f_{j,i})).toReal < ε (dist_edist, ENNReal.toReal_lt_of_lt_ofReal). So S_j ⊆ ⋃_{i∈F} ball(f_{j,i}, ε), a finite union of ε-balls with centres in S_j (Metric.totallyBounded_iff).
 (b) C_j is totally bounded (TotallyBounded.closure). It is closed in the complete space L_j, hence compact (TotallyBounded.isCompact_of_isClosed).

4. One subsequence for all j (Tychonoff form of the diagonal argument).
 (a) P := ∏_{j∈ℕ} C_j ⊆ X := ∏_{j∈ℕ} L_j is compact by Tychonoff (isCompact_univ_pi).
 (b) X is first countable: it is a countable product of metric, hence first-countable, spaces (Mathlib's FirstCountableTopology instance for countable products).
 (c) For every k, F_k := (f_{j,k})_{j∈ℕ} lies in P, since f_{j,k} ∈ S_j ⊆ C_j.
 (d) In a first-countable space, a sequence in a compact set has a subsequence converging to a point of that set (IsCompact.tendsto_subseq). So there are a ∈ P and a strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ with F_{ψ(k)} → a in X.
 (e) Convergence in a product is coordinatewise (tendsto_pi_nhds): f_{j,ψ(k)} → a_j in L_j as k → ∞, for every j.
 (Equivalent classical diagonal form, as in the parent proof. Choose strictly increasing φ_0 with f_{0,φ_0(k)} → g_0 in C_0 (IsCompact.tendsto_subseq) and put ψ_0 := φ_0. Recursively, choose strictly increasing φ_{j+1} with f_{j+1,ψ_j(φ_{j+1}(k))} → g_{j+1}, which is possible because k ↦ f_{j+1,ψ_j(k)} lies in C_{j+1}, and put ψ_{j+1} := ψ_j ∘ φ_{j+1}. The diagonal ψ(k) := ψ_k(k) is strictly increasing: φ_{k+1}(k+1) ≥ k+1 (StrictMono.id_le), so ψ(k+1) = ψ_k(φ_{k+1}(k+1)) ≥ ψ_k(k+1) > ψ_k(k) = ψ(k). Fix j. For k ≥ j, ψ(k) = ψ_j(m(k)) with m(k) := (φ_{j+1} ∘ ⋯ ∘ φ_k)(k). Since ψ and ψ_j are strictly increasing, m is strictly increasing on {k ≥ j}, so m(k) → ∞. Hence f_{j,ψ(k)} = f_{j,ψ_j(m(k))} → g_j. Taking a_j := g_j, either form proves 4(e).)

5. Conclusion. Put G_j := ⇑a_j, a representative of a_j ∈ L_j.
 (a) G_j is integrable on Q_j by 2(b).
 (b) By 2(b), ∫⁻_{Q_j} ‖u_{ψ(k)} − G_j‖ₑ = edist(f_{j,ψ(k)}, a_j) for every k.
 (c) By 4(e) and tendsto_iff_edist_tendsto_0, edist(f_{j,ψ(k)}, a_j) → 0. Hence ∫⁻_{Q_j} ‖u_{ψ(k)} − G_j‖ₑ → 0 for every j.
 (d) ψ is strictly increasing by 4(d). This proves the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: Embed f_{j,k} := [u_k]_{Q_j} into the complete space L_j = Lp ℝ 1 (volume.restrict Q_j), where edist(f_{j,k}, f_{j,i}) = ∫⁻_{Q_j}‖u_k − u_i‖ₑ (a.e.-strong measurability from integrability).
The finite nets make S_j = {f_{j,k}} totally bounded, so C_j = closure S_j is compact in the complete space L_j.

Tychonoff: ∏_j C_j is compact in the first-countable countable product ∏_j L_j, so IsCompact.tendsto_subseq gives one strictly increasing ψ with f_{j,ψ(k)} → a_j for every j; the nested-subsequence diagonal argument gives the same.
Set G_j := ⇑a_j; it is integrable on Q_j, ∫⁻_{Q_j}‖u_{ψ(k)} − G_j‖ₑ = edist(f_{j,ψ(k)}, a_j), and this tends to 0.

subproblems.title: Compatible L¹ limits on a cofinal compact exhaustion glue to an L¹_loc limit (steps 5–8 of the diagonal extraction)
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝⁿ open, Q_j ⊆ ℝⁿ (j ∈ ℕ) compact sets with Q_i ⊆ Q_j for i ≤ j such that every compact K ⊆ U is contained in some Q_j. Let w_k : ℝⁿ → ℝ (k ∈ ℕ) be functions that are a.e.-strongly measurable for Lebesgue measure restricted to each Q_j, and G_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ (j ∈ ℕ) functions with every G_j integrable on Q_j and ∫⁻_{Q_j} ‖w_k(x) − G_j(x)‖ₑ dx → 0 as k → ∞ for every j. Then there is v : ℝⁿ → ℝ, locally integrable on U, with ∫⁻_K ‖w_k(x) − v(x)‖ₑ dx → 0 for every compact K ⊆ U (SimonGMT Chapter02.TendstoLocallyInL1On w v U atTop).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (U : Set (Rn n)) (Q : ℕ → Set (Rn n)) (w G : ℕ → Rn n → ℝ), IsOpen U → (∀ j, IsCompact (Q j)) → Monotone Q → (∀ K : Set (Rn n), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ j, K ⊆ Q j) → (∀ j k, AEStronglyMeasurable (w k) (volume.restrict (Q j))) → (∀ j, IntegrableOn (G j) (Q j) volume) → (∀ j, Tendsto (fun k ↦ ∫⁻ x in Q j, ‖w k x - G j x‖ₑ) atTop (𝓝 0)) → ∃ v : Rn n → ℝ, LocallyIntegrableOn v U volume ∧ Chapter02.TendstoLocallyInL1On w v U atTop
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2, Theorem 2.6 (p. 50). The printed proof reduces the claim to precompactness in L¹_loc(U), and the reviewed proof supplied to node root.bv_results-a1.compactness-a1.diagonal_subseq-a1 (step A2 of root.bv_results-a1.compactness-a1) turns precompactness on every compact subset into an L¹_loc-convergent subsequence by compact exhaustion and diagonal extraction. This child is steps 5–8 of that proof (compatibility of the limits, gluing, convergence and local integrability), stated for an arbitrary monotone compact exhaustion Q_j that absorbs the compact subsets of U. Notation: μ = volume (Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ = Rn n); ∫⁻_A is the lower Lebesgue integral for μ.restrict A; ‖a‖ₑ is the extended norm; "a.e. on A" means μ.restrict A-a.e.

Hypotheses. (H0) U is open. (H1) Every Q_j is compact. (H2) Q is monotone: i ≤ j implies Q_i ⊆ Q_j. (H3) Every compact K ⊆ U lies in some Q_j. (H4) Every w_k is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ.restrict Q_j, for every j. (H5) Every G_j is integrable on Q_j. (H6) e_j(k) := ∫⁻_{Q_j} ‖w_k − G_j‖ₑ → 0 as k → ∞, for every j.
Claim. There is v : ℝⁿ → ℝ with LocallyIntegrableOn v U volume and ∫⁻_K ‖w_k − v‖ₑ → 0 for every compact K ⊆ U, i.e. Chapter02.TendstoLocallyInL1On w v U atTop.

0. Measurability. Each Q_j is compact, hence closed, hence a Borel and measurable set (IsCompact.isClosed, IsClosed.measurableSet).

1. Compatibility: for i ≤ j, G_i = G_j a.e. on Q_i.
 (a) Measurability. G_i is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ.restrict Q_i by (H5). G_j is a.e.-strongly measurable for μ.restrict Q_j by (H5), hence also for μ.restrict Q_i ≤ μ.restrict Q_j, since Q_i ⊆ Q_j by (H2) (AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_measure, Measure.restrict_mono).
 (b) Pointwise bound. For every k and x: G_i(x) − G_j(x) = (w_k(x) − G_j(x)) − (w_k(x) − G_i(x)). The triangle inequality for ‖·‖ₑ (enorm_sub_le) gives ‖G_i(x) − G_j(x)‖ₑ ≤ ‖w_k(x) − G_i(x)‖ₑ + ‖w_k(x) − G_j(x)‖ₑ.
 (c) Integral bound. Integrate (b) over Q_i (lintegral_mono). The lower integral is additive when one summand is a.e.-measurable (lintegral_add_left'). Here x ↦ ‖w_k(x) − G_i(x)‖ₑ is a.e.-measurable for μ.restrict Q_i by (H4) and (a). Then lintegral_mono_set with Q_i ⊆ Q_j gives
   ∫⁻_{Q_i} ‖G_i − G_j‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻_{Q_i} ‖w_k − G_i‖ₑ + ∫⁻_{Q_i} ‖w_k − G_j‖ₑ ≤ e_i(k) + e_j(k)   for every k.
 (d) The right side tends to 0 + 0 = 0 by (H6). The left side does not depend on k, so it is ≤ 0 (ge_of_tendsto'), i.e. ∫⁻_{Q_i} ‖G_i − G_j‖ₑ = 0.
 (e) The integrand is a.e.-measurable for μ.restrict Q_i by (a). By lintegral_eq_zero_iff', ‖G_i − G_j‖ₑ = 0, i.e. G_i = G_j, a.e. on Q_i.
 (This proof route uses (H4) exactly in the additivity step of (c). For functions that are not a.e.-measurable, the lower Lebesgue integral is superadditive but in general not subadditive. For example, let A ⊆ Q_i be such that A and Q_i ∖ A both have inner measure 0. Then ∫⁻_{Q_i} 1_A = ∫⁻_{Q_i} 1_{Q_i∖A} = 0, while ∫⁻_{Q_i} (1_A + 1_{Q_i∖A}) = μ(Q_i). The hypothesis is supplied by the parent, because each w_k = u_{ψ(k)} is integrable on every Q_j.)

2. Gluing. For x ∈ ⋃_j Q_j let j(x) be the least j with x ∈ Q_j (Nat.find) and put v(x) := G_{j(x)}(x). For x ∉ ⋃_j Q_j put v(x) := 0.
 Claim: for every j, v = G_j a.e. on Q_j. Fix j.
 (a) For each i ∈ ℕ, μ-a.e. x satisfies: i ≤ j and x ∈ Q_i imply G_i(x) = G_j(x). For i ≤ j this is step 1 converted from μ.restrict Q_i to μ with ae_restrict_iff' (Q_i is measurable by step 0). For i > j the statement is vacuous.
 (b) There are countably many i, so μ-a.e. x satisfies the statement of (a) for all i simultaneously (ae_all_iff).
 (c) Let x be such a point with x ∈ Q_j. Then x ∈ ⋃_i Q_i, so j(x) is defined. Also x ∈ Q_{j(x)} (Nat.find_spec) and j(x) ≤ j by minimality (Nat.find_min'). By (b), v(x) = G_{j(x)}(x) = G_j(x).
 (d) So μ-a.e. x satisfies x ∈ Q_j ⇒ v(x) = G_j(x). Since Q_j is measurable, ae_restrict_iff' turns this into v = G_j a.e. on Q_j.

3. Integrability on Q_j. G_j is integrable on Q_j (H5) and v = G_j a.e. on Q_j (step 2), so v is integrable on Q_j (IntegrableOn.congr_fun_ae).

4. Convergence. Let K ⊆ U be compact. By (H3) choose j with K ⊆ Q_j. For every k:
 (a) 0 ≤ ∫⁻_K ‖w_k − v‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻_{Q_j} ‖w_k − v‖ₑ (lintegral_mono_set).
 (b) ∫⁻_{Q_j} ‖w_k − v‖ₑ = ∫⁻_{Q_j} ‖w_k − G_j‖ₑ = e_j(k) (lintegral_congr_ae with step 2).
 (c) By (H6), e_j(k) → 0, so the squeeze theorem (tendsto_of_tendsto_of_tendsto_of_le_of_le) gives ∫⁻_K ‖w_k − v‖ₑ → 0.
 Since K was arbitrary, this is the definition of Chapter02.TendstoLocallyInL1On w v U atTop: for every compact K ⊆ U, Tendsto (fun k ↦ ∫⁻ x in K, ‖w k x − v x‖ₑ) atTop (𝓝 0).

5. Local integrability. Let K ⊆ U be compact. By (H3), K ⊆ Q_j for some j, so v is integrable on K by step 3 and IntegrableOn.mono_set. U is open (H0), hence locally closed (IsOpen.isLocallyClosed), and ℝⁿ is locally compact. So locallyIntegrableOn_iff gives LocallyIntegrableOn v U volume.

6. Steps 4 and 5 prove the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: Compatibility: for i ≤ j, ∫⁻_{Q_i}‖G_i − G_j‖ₑ ≤ e_i(k) + e_j(k) → 0 by the triangle inequality, additivity of ∫⁻ (using a.e.-measurability of w_k) and Q_i ⊆ Q_j; so G_i = G_j a.e. on Q_i.
Gluing: v(x) := G_{j(x)}(x) with j(x) the least j such that x ∈ Q_j, and v := 0 off ⋃_j Q_j; countably many null sets give v = G_j a.e. on Q_j.
v is integrable on every Q_j (IntegrableOn.congr_fun_ae).
For compact K ⊆ Q_j ⊆ U: ∫⁻_K‖w_k − v‖ₑ ≤ ∫⁻_{Q_j}‖w_k − v‖ₑ = e_j(k) → 0, which gives TendstoLocallyInL1On w v U atTop.
v is integrable on every compact K ⊆ U and U is open, so LocallyIntegrableOn v U volume (locallyIntegrableOn_iff).
